sourceRefs.locator: AA00016037/00033, typescript pp. 1–3, scans image0096–image0098. Page 1 gives his Colón address and Panamanian citizenship, recalls Bajo Matachín, names Marian Cunningson and Caroline Lowe and prices their breakfast. Page 2 records 18 years as an artisan and 30 on deck, and his tally of 5,330 transits.

AA00016037/00001, scans image0003–image0004, ‘The Contest’ and ‘The Entries’, for the circular sent to fifteen newspapers, relief packages, posting deadline and anniversary. List of entrants on image0005 and image0007 includes Clarke and Simmons.

Modern American History 7 (1), pp. 127–130, especially pp. 127 and 130. The author identifies the 112 written testimonies in Box 25 of the Isthmian Historical Society collection at the Library of Congress and discusses how they were solicited and kept.
TGN 7006458, coordinates 9.3500 N, 79.9000 W, Aspinwall as alternative name, historical note on the northern terminus. City-level point on Manzanillo Island.

labels.en: What Clarke wrote down in Colón

note.de: In seiner Einsendung für den Wettbewerb von 1963 erinnert sich Amos E. Clarke aus Colón an Marian Cunningson und Caroline Lowe, die Jahre zuvor Arbeiter in Bajo Matachín mit Frühstück versorgten.
note.en: Writing from Colón for the 1963 competition, Amos E. Clarke recalls Marian Cunningson and Caroline Lowe, who sold breakfast to canal workers many years earlier at Bajo Matachín.
